article.headline: PSG's 12-game winning streak halted by home draw against Roma
article.description: Paris Saint-Germain's 12-game winning streak ended Wednesday with a 2-2 Champions League draw against Roma.
article.linkText: Roma end PSG's 12-game winning run with Champions League draw in Paris
article.story:
Paris Saint-Germain dropped points for the first time in this season's Champions League as they were held to a 2-2 draw at home to AS Roma.

Illia Zabarnyi's header and Ousmane Dembele's penalty gave PSG the advantage in Paris after Mario Hermoso's opener but Donyell Malen scored from the spot to earn Roma an impressive point against the reigning champions.

The draw ended PSG's 12-game winning run in all competitions and meant they failed to join Real Madrid in making it five Champions League wins from five.

PSG's quest for a third successive Champions League crown has been hit in recent weeks by ACL injuries to star forwards Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, against Barcelona last month, and Désiré Doué during Saturday's win over Nice.

Luis Enrique left Ousmane Dembélé on the bench while Gian Piero Gasperini heavily rotated his Roma side, with Paulo Dybala, Malen and Bryan Cristante all kept in reserve.

Home fans at the Parc des Princes welcomed their visitors from the Italian capital with a huge tifo depicting two gladiators but it was Roma who were immediately up for the fight.

Matìas Soulè charged down the left and cut back from the byline for marauding centre-back Hermoso, who fired in from seven yards after just five minutes.

Roma have surrendered winning positions late on against Real Madrid and Manchester United already in this season's competition and PSG sought an an immediate response but Nuno Mendes was denied by Mile Svilar.

Roma were undone by a corner in the 31st minute. Zabarnyi was left unmarked at the near post and the former Bournemouth defender flicked in his first Champions League goal to draw the hosts level.

Evan Ndicka passed up a golden chance to restore Roma's lead six minutes before half-time but the centre-back's glancing header from a corner was just wide.

Hermoso had another golden chance but volleyed over from inside the area after goalkeeper Matvey Safonov flapped at Wesley's cross.

Niccolò Pisilli then drew a superb low stop from Safonov as PSG continued to come under fire but down the other end Joao Neves' diving header was off target from close range.

Luis Enrique turned to Dembele and Warren Zaïre-Emery just before the hour mark.

And they immediately created their chance as Achraf Hakimi burst in behind and was hauled back by Wesley as he charged into the area, with referee Glenn Nyberg pointing to the spot but opting only to give the Roma defender a yellow card.

Dembele's second touch after coming on was to take the spot-kick and he sent Svilar the wrong way to score his fourth goal of the competition.

But Roma were not daunted as they hit PSG on the break after 74 minutes and substitute Malen's ball across fell to Soule - whose effort struck the hand of Vitinha. Following a lengthy VAR check, a penalty was awarded and Malen - who scored four goals in the Serie A match against Parma at the weekend - made no mistake.

Fabián Ruiz had two efforts blocked and Dembele was denied by Svilar as Roma held on to pick up their fifth point.
